evaluated.name: DiscretionaryAccrualFragilityAmplifier

evaluated.name: PeakAccrualsFacingMaturityWall
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), 5), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(re, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accruals reverse when they are extreme relative to the firm's own history, and the reversal is most costly when a large share of the firm's liabilities comes due within a year and its accumulated earnings cushion against those liabilities is thin.

The distress leg is deliberately refinancing-specific — short-term debt as a share of total liabilities plus a retained-earnings-to-liabilities deficit — so it identifies firms that must roll debt precisely when the accrual reversal hits reported earnings, a different conditioning variable from the leverage/deficit level used in the accepted amplifier.

evaluated.hypothesis: Static distress is visible and largely priced; what investors underweight is the trajectory, so accrual-inflated earnings are most dangerous in firms whose leverage has been ratcheting upward over several years, because that is where management is actively defending reported numbers while the balance sheet erodes.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the MIN gate with a trend-based conditioner changes the economic claim rather than the aggregation algebra: the question is now whether the accrual anomaly is amplified by deteriorating solvency dynamics as opposed to the distress level, which is directly testable against the accepted level-based amplifier and cannot be highly correlated with it by construction. RANK of the three-year leverage trend is a smooth, non-negative intensity that preserves all information in both legs, avoids any mass point, and requires only three years of history so coverage stays high.

evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), MAX(ceq, dp))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm whose accumulated soft operating assets already exceed its book equity cushion cannot absorb a write-down without impairing solvency, so additional accrual building in that state is the most dangerous configuration on the balance sheet.
evaluated.reasoning: The equity-cushion ratio delivered the archive's strongest FMB slope but negligible alpha, the signature of a sound cross-sectional relation whose extreme quintiles are captured by tiny-denominator firms; converting the cushion-relative bloat into a ranked gate on the signed accrual flow preserves the economics while making portfolio formation stable. The deflator is floored at one year's depreciation so negative-book-equity firms sit at the fragile end rather than being sign-flipped into the long leg.

evaluated.name: AccrualsAtOwnHistoricalLeveragePeak

evaluated.hypothesis: Distress is firm-specific: a utility at 60% leverage is normal while a software firm at 30% is stressed, so the relevant state is whether the firm sits at the top of its *own* five-year leverage distribution, which marks a regime its managers and creditors treat as abnormal.
evaluated.reasoning: Every leverage gate in the archive is cross-sectional, so structural industry and business-model differences contaminate who gets classified as fragile; a within-firm time-series rank removes all fixed firm and industry effects and identifies stress from the firm's own baseline. evaluated.name: SupplierCreditWithdrawalUnderLeveredDrain
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(NEG(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(che, dp), lt), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The liability half of the working-capital accrual is a supplier-credit signal: a firm whose non-debt current liabilities are shrinking is repaying trade credit faster, which for a levered firm with deteriorating internal liquidity means suppliers have tightened terms rather than that the firm chose to deleverage.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic was right that my previous version double-subtracted depreciation and therefore was not the algebraic complement of the archived asset-side leg; this version uses −Δ(lct − dlc) alone, which is exactly the component the asset-side test discarded, so the two halves now reconcile to the net measure. Depreciation instead enters the liquidity gate, where it belongs economically — cash plus non-cash charge capacity measures the internal resources available to meet obligations — so it plays a non-redundant role rather than cancelling.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWhenDebtOutstripsHardAssetBase
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(lt, dp), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Leverage measured against total assets is contaminated by the very soft assets accruals inflate, so the honest measure of debt capacity exhaustion is liabilities per dollar of hard, depreciating asset base — the collateral creditors can actually seize and redeploy.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic industry-rank swap with a diagnostic that separates two specific confounds: lt/at falls mechanically when a firm books soft assets, so the archived gate partially anti-selects the very firms the hypothesis targets, while lt/dp is immune to that channel and simultaneously captures the collateral-quality dimension that varies across asset technologies. If the alpha strengthens relative to the lt/at gate, the winning gate was being diluted by accrual-driven denominator inflation; if it weakens, we learn total-asset leverage was capturing scale rather than collateral, and the winsorized ratio keeps low-depreciation firms from dominating the tail.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWithinOneShockOfALoss
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ABS(pi), VOL(ni, 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Proximity to the loss threshold should be measured in units of the firm's own earnings uncertainty: a firm earning a small profit with very stable income is safe, whereas one earning the same profit with volatile income is a single ordinary shock away from a reported loss and has every incentive to build a reserve of accruals now.
evaluated.reasoning: All archived threshold gates deflate pretax income by a balance-sheet scale (assets or liabilities), which conflates proximity to breakeven with firm size and capital structure; dividing by the five-year volatility of net income creates a distance-to-loss statistic directly analogous to distance-to-default and is the economically correct normalization for a threshold mechanism. Coverage will fall because of the five-year window, which must be weighed against any improvement in alpha.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWhenEquityIsFewShocksFromZero
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ceq, VOL(ni, 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Solvency risk is the size of the equity cushion relative to the size of the shocks that erode it, so the fragile firms are those whose book equity amounts to only a few years of typical earnings variation — precisely the firms for which a soft-asset write-down is existential.
evaluated.reasoning: Every leverage gate in the archive is a static ratio of two balance-sheet stocks and therefore treats a stable utility and a volatile cyclical with identical leverage as equally fragile, which is economically wrong; scaling the cushion by earnings volatility introduces the risk dimension the archive has never used. It is also structurally different from Signal 2, which measures distance to a reporting threshold rather than distance to insolvency, so the pair separates the earnings-management motive from genuine default risk.

evaluated.name: AccrualsInOperationallyLeveredDrainingFirms
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(dp, sale)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Fragility is not only financial: firms carrying heavy fixed capital charges per dollar of revenue cannot shrink costs when demand weakens, so a working-capital build financed out of a draining cash cushion is far more likely to end in write-downs for them than for asset-light firms with flexible cost structures.
evaluated.reasoning: Every gate tested so far measures financial obligations, while operating leverage — the fixed-cost side of distress risk — has never entered, making this the batch's genuinely new economic channel rather than another liability ratio. Depreciation per dollar of sales is the natural fixed-charge intensity measure available in this menu, and pairing it with the established liquidity-drain trigger keeps the comparison to the archived gate clean.

evaluated.name: AccrualBuildPerDollarOfReportedProfit
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), MAX(ABS(pi), dp)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is how large the accrual build is relative to the profit it is supporting: when a year's working-capital build dwarfs reported pretax income, the earnings number is essentially a bookkeeping residual, and this is automatically most extreme for firms hovering near breakeven.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of multiplying the archived accrual leg by the archived breakeven gate — which the critic rightly called a mechanical conjunction — this embeds the threshold mechanism inside the deflator, so the interaction is intrinsic to a single quantity and the resulting signal is not a rank-multiplication of two existing series. Flooring the denominator at one year's depreciation and taking absolute pretax income keeps the measure finite and correctly signed for loss-making firms, which is exactly the tail problem that crippled the earlier cushion-deflated ratio.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWhenTangibleCushionIsGone
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The cushion that actually protects creditors is book equity after the soft working-capital assets are written off; firms whose tangible-of-accruals equity is small or negative relative to obligations have no loss absorption left, so any further accrual build is being layered on an already-exhausted balance sheet.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes exactly one thing relative to the archive — the distress state — and it is a state no prior signal contains: equity net of soft assets rather than raw equity, leverage, or cash. Because the deduction of accumulated soft assets from equity is a level while the signal leg is a one-year flow, the two are not mechanically coupled, and unlike the flagged proposal it does not stack an archived gate onto a re-scaled archived leg.

evaluated.name: AccrualsUnvalidatedByTaxAuthorities

evaluated.hypothesis: Tax expense is an independent, costly-to-manipulate validation of reported income, so a firm booking profits while recognizing almost no tax is either running on loss carryforwards or reporting income the tax authorities do not see — and an accrual build in that state is the classic low-quality-earnings configuration.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the two-threshold conjunction the critic rejected and opens the one channel the archive has never used, the tax variable txt, which supplies external corroboration of earnings rather than another liability-scaled balance-sheet ratio and therefore cannot reselect the same small-liability population. Flooring the denominator at annual depreciation makes the effective-tax measure well behaved for loss firms and near-zero-income firms, so the gate is a smooth non-negative intensity that keeps the signed accrual leg's long-short structure intact.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWhenLastYearsTangibleCushionWasGone
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(LAG(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1), lt))))

Lagging the cushion by one year breaks the same-year identity while preserving the economics, so a surviving alpha validates the mechanism and a collapse tells the final generation to prefer the breakeven and levered-drain gates instead.

evaluated.name: AccrualsAsAssetProductivityCollapses
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A multi-year decline in sales generated per dollar of assets means the asset base is becoming unproductive — inventory is not moving and receivables are not converting — so accrual builds during that decline represent assets the business can no longer turn into cash.
evaluated.reasoning: Asset turnover is the one classic Altman distress component the archive has never used, and it is conceptually distinct from every gate tested: it measures operational deterioration rather than financing stress, liquidity, or reporting incentives. The three-year trend form is the construction that has repeatedly worked in this archive, and unlike the failed one-year sales-growth conditioner it captures persistent productivity decay rather than a transitory demand shock.

evaluated.name: AccrualsOfBarelyProfitableFirms
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(pi, lt)))), INDICATOR(pi, 0)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The threshold mechanism is asymmetric: a firm reporting a small profit is one that plausibly managed its way across the zero line, whereas a firm reporting a small loss has already conceded the benchmark and has less to defend, so the accrual penalty should be concentrated on the profitable side of the threshold.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's best signal treats firms symmetrically around zero, but the earnings-management literature's benchmark logic is explicitly one-sided, and testing that asymmetry is a genuine economic claim rather than a rescaling. The indicator zeroes only the loss-making minority, so the surviving continuous variation still populates both extreme quintiles, and a stronger alpha would establish that the archive's threshold result is driven by benchmark-beating rather than by generic proximity to zero income.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWhileBorrowingExceedsEarnings
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(lt, 1), at), RATIO(pi, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm whose liabilities grew by far more than it earned during the year is filling an external funding gap; accrual builds financed by that gap are soft assets purchased with borrowed money rather than with operating profit.
evaluated.reasoning: Every financing gate in the archive measures either the stock of debt, its trend, or its maturity, never the contemporaneous shortfall between what the firm earned and what it borrowed, which is the flow that actually reveals dependence on external capital. Differencing the two asset-scaled quantities creates a single funding-gap measure whose high end contains firms adding obligations while generating little or negative income, a state distinct from both high leverage and low liquidity.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWhenDebtIsReclassifiedAsCurrent
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(dltt, at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: When a borrower breaches a covenant, accountants must reclassify long-term debt as currently due, so a year in which short-term debt rises while long-term debt falls by a similar amount is a visible fingerprint of technical default — and accrual builds reported in such a year are the least credible in the cross-section.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the deflator-permutation search the critic rightly rejected and instead targets a discrete distress *event* rather than a continuous state, which no gate in the archive attempts. Differencing the change in short-term debt against the change in long-term debt distinguishes reclassification (the distress fingerprint) from ordinary new short-term borrowing, which the previously tested Δ(dlc/lt) gate conflated, and both components are asset-scaled so no near-zero denominator arises.

evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(dp, sale))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))

evaluated.name: AccrualsInChronicallyMarginalFirms
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(MA(pi, 3), lt)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year at breakeven can be a transitory shock, whereas three consecutive years of income hovering near zero against a large liability stack describes a zombie firm surviving on creditor forbearance, where accrual management is chronic rather than opportunistic.
evaluated.reasoning: Every threshold gate tested so far uses a one-year snapshot of pretax income, so persistence of marginality — the distinction between a bad year and a structurally non-viable business — has never been examined despite the archive repeatedly showing that multi-year states outperform single-year ones. Smoothing pretax income over three years also removes transitory items that make |pi| a noisy proximity measure, which should sharpen the gate without materially reducing coverage.

evaluated.name: AbnormalVersusOwnAccrualNormAtBreakeven
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 3))), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(pi, lt)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms differ permanently in how much working capital their business model requires, so the discretionary component is the deviation of this year's build from the firm's own recent norm, and it is that deviation which should reverse when a breakeven firm can no longer carry it.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg in the archive is a raw cross-sectional level, which conflates a distributor's structurally high working-capital intensity with an opportunistic build; demeaning by the firm's own three-year average removes the firm fixed effect that industry adjustment failed to remove in generation 2. Pairing this cleaner leg with the archive's best gate isolates the leg-side design choice, and if it improves both metrics it identifies within-firm abnormality as the true carrier of the interaction.

evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at), RATIO(pi, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm raising contractual debt far in excess of what it earned is closing an external funding gap on terms that must be serviced, and accrual builds financed out of that gap are soft assets bought with borrowed money.

evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(che, lt), 5), RATIO(che, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What marks a firm as liquidity-stressed is not the direction of this year's cash change but how far its cash cushion has fallen from the best level it has sustained in recent memory, since that peak reveals the buffer the business itself judged necessary.

evaluated.name: AccrualsWhileStretchingTaxPayments
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(txp, lt), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Taxes owed but unpaid are the one liability a firm cannot negotiate away, so a rising balance of accrued taxes relative to total obligations signals that cash is being conserved at the expense of a non-negotiable creditor — a strain marker that precedes visible default risk.

evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The danger of a soft-asset build depends on how quickly those assets convert to cash: a firm already carrying many months of sales tied up in receivables and inventory has a slow, congested operating cycle, so an additional build is far more likely to end in markdowns than in collections.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has scaled the soft-asset stock by liabilities and by the equity cushion but never by revenue, and the revenue scaling measures something economically different — the conversion period of the operating cycle rather than solvency coverage — which is the mechanism that determines whether an accrual reverses through cash collection or through write-off. It therefore complements rather than interpolates the tested gates, and using a stock-to-flow ratio avoids both the small-denominator instability of the cushion ratio and the payables contamination of the liability-scaled gates.

Low-accrual, low-fragility firms sit near zero rather than being forced to the long leg, isolating the interaction rather than either main effect. Retained earnings enter negatively so that accumulated-loss firms are ranked as more distressed.

considered.hypothesis: Poor accrual quality (unstable, noisy accruals) is only weakly priced on its own, but for firms whose operating cash flow barely covers liabilities it signals opaque, unreliable earnings and elevated default risk that investors underweight.

considered.name: WorkingCapitalStrainUnderIlliquidity
considered.expression: MUL(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), RATIO(lct, act))
considered.hypothesis: Growth in non-cash working capital drains liquidity; for firms whose current liabilities already crowd their current assets, this drain is a direct precursor of funding stress and forced earnings reversal.
considered.reasoning: The first term is the classic balance-sheet working-capital accrual (receivables plus inventory less non-debt current liabilities), and the second is the inverse current ratio, a canonical liquidity-distress measure that scales up the penalty when the buffer is thin. considered.name: AccrualEscalationWithLeveringUp
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: What matters is deterioration dynamics, not static states: a firm that is simultaneously widening the gap between reported earnings and operating cash flow while adding leverage is funding a shortfall with debt and smoothing the optics, and this joint deterioration predicts negative abnormal returns beyond either level effect.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the hard leverage indicator with a continuous rank of the change in leverage removes the degenerate mass at zero and gives every firm a defined score, so quintile breakpoints are well populated and the spread is not driven by tie-breaking. considered.name: AccrualCashConjunctionGate
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual overstatement is punished only when the firm lacks the cash reserves to absorb the eventual reversal; the penalty is conjunctive, so a firm must be both accrual-heavy and cash-poor relative to its obligations to be in the short leg.
considered.reasoning: MIN of the two ranks is a strict conjunction that scores high only when both conditions bind, which is a different functional form from a product or a sum and cannot be reproduced by either theme alone, while remaining continuous on the unit interval with full coverage. The deflator problem is eliminated: accruals are scaled by total assets as usual, and the distress leg uses cash to total liabilities, whose components (che, lt levels) are not the accrual numerator's own flow items, so there is no mechanical numerator-denominator link.

considered.name: ChronicAccrualsUnderRefinancingRisk
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, at), NEG(RATIO(che, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that have reported income above operating cash flow for several consecutive years have built a stock of unreversed accruals; when they also face near-term debt maturities with thin cash reserves, the refinancing constraint forces the reversal into the open and returns underperform.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the mis-specified book-tax construction entirely and replaces it with a cumulative three-year accrual stock, which is a persistence concept rather than a profitability level and therefore carries no implicit contradiction with the profitability premium. The distress leg is deliberately refinancing-specific (short-term debt intensity plus cash shortfall against liabilities) rather than generic leverage, giving a channel distinct from the accepted signals while keeping coverage high since only three years of data are required.

considered.hypothesis: Adding back depreciation isolates the working-capital, managerially discretionary part of accruals; this component is the one that reverses badly, and its reversal is most damaging for firms with high leverage and depleted retained earnings.
considered.reasoning: Total accruals mix a non-discretionary depreciation charge (driven by past capex, not reporting choice) with the discretionary working-capital build, so removing it should raise signal-to-noise relative to the Sloan main effect. considered.expression: MUL(VOL(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), 5), SUMRANK(RATIO(lt, at), NEG(RATIO(ni, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Unstable discretionary accruals proxy for opaque, low-quality earnings; opacity is priced only when the firm's earnings barely cover its liability stock, because that is where information risk translates into real default risk.

considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), sale)), SUMRANK(RATIO(lt, at), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Distressed firms facing revenue pressure loosen credit terms and stuff the channel, so receivables and inventory grow out of proportion to sales; this specific accrual component, not accruals in general, carries the earnings-management content for fragile firms.
