considered.name: DepreciationSlowdownUnderDebtLoad
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dp, at), 1))), SUMRANK(RATIO(dltt, at), NEG(RATIO(pi, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Long-lived-asset accruals are also discretionary: a firm that quietly slows its depreciation rate boosts reported earnings without cash, and this cosmetic choice is most likely and most misleading when long-term debt is heavy and pretax income is thin.
considered.reasoning: This targets the non-working-capital accrual margin, a channel none of the other proposals touch, so it diversifies the batch's economic content rather than its formula shape. A falling depreciation-to-assets ratio is sign-flipped so that higher values mean more aggressive reporting, and the long-term-debt-plus-weak-pretax-income multiplier restricts the effect to firms with a motive to manage reported earnings for creditors.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PeakAccrualsFacingMaturityWall
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), 5), SUMRANK(RATIO(dlc, lt), NEG(RATIO(re, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Accruals reverse when they are extreme relative to the firm's own history, and the reversal is most costly when a large share of the firm's liabilities comes due within a year and its accumulated earnings cushion against those liabilities is thin.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the tax-payable construction whose sign contradicted the accrual channel and replaces it with an unambiguous reversal-timing mechanism: TS_RANK measures where current discretionary accruals sit within the firm's own five-year distribution, so it removes stable firm-level accrual differences and isolates the transient build that must unwind. The distress leg is deliberately refinancing-specific — short-term debt as a share of total liabilities plus a retained-earnings-to-liabilities deficit — so it identifies firms that must roll debt precisely when the accrual reversal hits reported earnings, a different conditioning variable from the leverage/deficit level used in the accepted amplifier.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhileSolvencyDeteriorates
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(lt, at), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Static distress is visible and largely priced; what investors underweight is the trajectory, so accrual-inflated earnings are most dangerous in firms whose leverage has been ratcheting upward over several years, because that is where management is actively defending reported numbers while the balance sheet erodes.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the MIN gate with a trend-based conditioner changes the economic claim rather than the aggregation algebra: the question is now whether the accrual anomaly is amplified by deteriorating solvency dynamics as opposed to the distress level, which is directly testable against the accepted level-based amplifier and cannot be highly correlated with it by construction. RANK of the three-year leverage trend is a smooth, non-negative intensity that preserves all information in both legs, avoids any mass point, and requires only three years of history so coverage stays high.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BalanceSheetAccrualsWhileLeveringUp
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(lt, at), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual-inflated earnings are most dangerous in firms whose leverage has been ratcheting upward for several years, because that is where management is defending reported numbers while the balance sheet erodes; the effect should be stronger and better measured with a full-sample accrual definition.
considered.reasoning: This keeps the only conditioning variable that produced a reliable FF5 alpha (−3.8%/yr, t = −2.83) but replaces the cash-flow-statement accrual core with the balance-sheet construction Δ(AR+INV−AP) − depreciation, which needs no oancf and should roughly double coverage. If the alpha survives with materially higher coverage it becomes a credible result rather than a small-sample artifact, and if it collapses we learn the earlier alpha was driven by the post-1988 oancf subsample.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsAsEquityCushionErodes
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(re, at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: The operative deterioration is the burning of accumulated earnings, not the addition of debt: firms whose retained-earnings base has been shrinking for years are running out of internal cushion, so their accrual builds are far more likely to be reversal-bound window dressing.
considered.reasoning: This isolates a specific design choice against Signal 1 — same accrual core, same trend horizon, but the trajectory is measured on the equity-cushion side rather than the debt side — so the pair identifies which limb of the deterioration story carries the alpha. Retained-earnings erosion also captures loss-making histories that leverage ratios miss for asset-light firms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildAsCashCushionDrains
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A working-capital accrual build is a cash drain; it becomes a distress signal only when the firm's cash reserves relative to its obligations are simultaneously falling, because that combination means the build is being financed out of a shrinking liquidity buffer rather than out of slack.
considered.reasoning: This makes the interaction contemporaneous and flow-based — accrual build meets liquidity depletion in the same year — rather than pairing a flow with a stock, which is the design flaw shared by most of the archive. It tests whether the deterioration effect in Signal 1 is really about debt or about the cash cushion being consumed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IndustryExcessAccrualsInFragileFirms
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(lt, at), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Normal accrual levels are an industry technology (retailers carry inventory, service firms do not), so only the deviation from industry norms is discretionary; that excess accrual is what should be punished in fragile firms.
considered.reasoning: The level-based composites in gen 1 produced essentially zero alpha, and a plausible reason is that raw accrual ranks are dominated by industry business models that also correlate with leverage, muddying the interaction. Industry-demeaning the accrual leg while keeping the fragility intensity tests whether purging that confound rescues the level-conditioned version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WorkingCapitalBuildFundedByShortDebt
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The funding source matters: a working-capital accrual build financed by a shift toward short-maturity debt creates a maturity mismatch, since illiquid receivables and inventory are being carried on liabilities that must be rolled within the year.
considered.reasoning: This proposes a maturity-structure channel rather than a leverage-level or leverage-trend channel, so it is economically separable from Signals 1 and 2 even though it shares the accrual core. The conditioner is the change in the short-term share of total liabilities, which rises when banks shorten terms on weakening borrowers, making it a market-validated distress signal rather than an accounting ratio.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PersistentUnderDepreciationInShrinkingLeveredFirms
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(at, 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(lt, at), NEG(RATIO(pi, lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: A multi-year downward drift in depreciation intensity inside a firm that is not expanding its asset base cannot be explained by new investment; it points to stretched useful lives or delayed write-downs, and this earnings-flattering choice is most likely in levered firms with thin pretax income.
considered.reasoning: The critic's objection was that any linear difference of growth rates loads positively on asset growth, so the previous construction could be a relabelled investment-factor result; here the conditioner deliberately loads on *low* asset growth, meaning a negative slope runs against the asset-growth anomaly rather than mimicking it. Using a five-year TREND in dp/at rather than a one-year change also filters out transient capex-timing effects, leaving persistent depreciation-policy drift, and the fragility legs (leverage, weak pretax income relative to liabilities) supply the distress conditioning the theme requires.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildAfterMultiYearCashErosion
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(che, lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: What conditions the accrual effect is a pre-existing, multi-year erosion of the cash cushion relative to obligations, not the mechanical same-year cash decline that any working-capital build must produce.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that in AccrualBuildAsCashCushionDrains the two legs are coupled through the cash-flow identity, so the winning result could be a near-quadratic in accruals rather than genuine conditioning. Replacing the contemporaneous ΔCash/LT with a three-year trend breaks the same-year accounting link while preserving the economics, so if the alpha survives the conditioning interpretation is vindicated and if it vanishes we have diagnosed the artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildWithoutDemandInLeveredFirms
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1)), RATIO(lt, at)))
considered.hypothesis: Receivable and inventory builds are benign when revenue is expanding to justify them; when sales are shrinking and the firm is levered, the same build means unsold goods and uncollectible credit sales rather than growth investment.
considered.reasoning: This introduces a real-activity validation channel absent from the archive: the conditioner asks whether the working-capital build is corroborated by demand, which is exactly the discriminator between growth-driven and manipulation-driven accruals. Pairing sales contraction with leverage keeps the distress content while giving an economically different limb from cash, retained earnings, and debt-maturity conditioners.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ChronicAccrualStockMeetsLiquidityDrain
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), 3), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A single year of accrual build can be operational noise; three consecutive years of unreversed build creates a stock of soft assets that must eventually be written down, and the write-down is forced when liquidity is draining.
considered.reasoning: This changes the accrual leg from a one-year flow to a cumulative stock, testing whether persistence rather than magnitude is what interacts with fragility, and it addresses the coupling concern differently from Signal 2 since two of the three summed years precede the current cash decline. It is a substantive timing hypothesis rather than a rescaling of the winner.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildAsCoverageCapacityFades
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(pi, lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Distress ultimately means the earnings stream can no longer service the liability stack; a multi-year decline in pretax income relative to total liabilities marks that erosion of debt-service capacity, and accrual builds occurring during it are most likely to be earnings support rather than genuine growth.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested so far is balance-sheet based (cash, leverage, retained earnings, debt maturity); this substitutes a flow-based coverage measure, which is the variable creditors actually monitor and the one that triggers covenant renegotiation. If income-based deterioration conditions the accrual effect as strongly as balance-sheet deterioration, the mechanism generalizes; if not, it localizes the story to liquidity rather than profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OpaqueAccrualsMeetLiquidityDrain
considered.expression: MUL(VOL(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 5), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose accruals swing erratically have low-quality, hard-to-verify earnings; that opacity is priced only when cash reserves relative to obligations are actually falling, because that is when investors must rely on the unreliable numbers to assess solvency.
considered.reasoning: The gen-1 opacity test used the oancf-based core and a static distress level and produced a weak −1.8% alpha at 8% coverage; this rebuilds it on the balance-sheet core (higher coverage, no oancf) and pairs it with the dynamic conditioner that has actually worked, so it is a properly powered test of the information-risk channel rather than a repeat. Both legs are non-negative and increasing in badness, keeping the sign logic clean.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildAsDebtOutgrowsRevenue
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(lt, sale), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Solvency is ultimately about whether the business can grow into its obligations, so a multi-year rise in liabilities per dollar of revenue marks a firm losing that race; accrual builds occurring while debt-per-revenue climbs are earnings support for a shrinking commercial base rather than investment in a growing one.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the rank-average ensemble with a single new conditioning concept — revenue-scaled debt burden — that is economically separable from the archived asset-scaled leverage trend, because a firm with stable lt/at but collapsing sales shows nothing on the asset-based measure yet is clearly losing debt-service capacity. It is also distinct from the accepted sales-growth conditioner, which uses a one-year demand shock plus a static leverage level, whereas this measures a persistent three-year deterioration in the debt-to-revenue relationship.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SalesAdjustedAccrualsUnderLiquidityDrain
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), ZSCORE(GROWTH(sale, 1))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Working-capital growth that is proportional to revenue growth is mechanical and benign; only the component unexplained by sales expansion is discretionary, and it is that abnormal component whose reversal is forced when liquidity is draining.
considered.reasoning: The gen-3 demand test failed because sales information was put in the conditioner, where it competes with the fragility measure; the Jones-model logic says it belongs in the accrual leg as a normalization. Subtracting standardized sales growth from the standardized accrual creates an abnormal-accrual measure while retaining the conditioner that has worked, which should sharpen both the slope and the spread if the manipulation interpretation is right.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DeteriorationOnlyBitesWhenAlreadyLevered
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Distress level and distress deterioration are not substitutes but complements: losing liquidity is survivable for an unlevered firm and existential for a levered one, so the accrual penalty should be concentrated where a high debt load meets a shrinking cash cushion.
considered.reasoning: Levels alone produced zero alpha and deterioration alone produced −3.1%, and the untested economic claim is that the level *gates* the deterioration rather than adding to it — a multiplicative gate, not the rank-average ensemble the critic rejected. If the alpha strengthens, the mechanism is a genuine three-way interaction; if it weakens, we learn deterioration works uniformly across the leverage distribution, which is itself an informative constraint on the story.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildAsNetLiquidityGapWidens
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lt), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: What matters is cash net of debt that must be repaid within the year: a firm whose cash minus short-term debt is deteriorating relative to total obligations has no discretionary liquidity left, which is precisely when soft assets must be liquidated or written down.
considered.reasoning: Raw cash overstates available liquidity for firms with large maturing balances, so netting current debt out of the cash position is an economically sharper distress state than the archived che/lt drain, not merely a rescaling. It also separates the liquidity story from the maturity-mismatch story tested earlier by putting both elements in one net-position measure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhileInterestBearingDebtRises
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine solvency deterioration means taking on more interest-bearing borrowing; a rise in total liabilities driven by payables is itself an accrual event, so the debt-based conditioning should be tested on financial debt alone.
considered.reasoning: The archive's leverage-trend conditioner uses lt, which contains accounts payable — the same item that enters the accrual leg with the opposite sign — so part of the −2.2% alpha could be an accounting-identity artifact rather than a distress interaction. Restricting the conditioner to dltt + dlc removes that overlap entirely, making this a clean identification test whose failure or success materially changes how we interpret the whole leverage-trend family.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildAtWorkingCapitalCovenantEdge
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Bank loan agreements routinely impose a current-ratio or minimum-working-capital covenant, so firms whose net working capital sits near zero relative to their obligations are at the covenant edge, where the incentive to inflate receivables and inventory is strongest and the consequence of a reversal — technical default — is most severe.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested so far is monotone in distress, but covenant pressure is inherently non-monotone: firms with comfortably positive working capital face no constraint, and deeply negative-working-capital firms have already breached and been renegotiated, so the danger zone is the neighbourhood of zero. Using the absolute distance of net working capital from zero, scaled by total liabilities, gives a genuinely new economic conditioning variable rather than a preprocessing change to an existing signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SoftCollateralAgainstHardObligations
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), lt), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Creditors lend against verifiable, redeployable assets; a firm whose liabilities are backed mainly by receivables and inventory rather than depreciable fixed assets holds soft collateral that loses most of its value precisely in the states where it must be pledged or liquidated.
considered.reasoning: This shifts the accrual leg from a one-year flow to the *stock* of accrual-based assets expressed per dollar of obligations, and pairs it with the absence of hard-asset backing measured by depreciation intensity relative to liabilities, so the claim is about balance-sheet composition and collateral quality rather than about deterioration dynamics. It is therefore not a recombination of the archive's best legs — neither a working-capital accrual flow nor a deterioration trend appears — and it supplies the theme interaction through the shared lt deflator that makes both legs solvency-relative.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetSideAccrualsGatedByLeveredDrain
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: The manipulable, reversal-prone accruals are on the asset side — receivables and inventory the firm chooses to recognize — whereas payables are supplier decisions; isolating the asset side should preserve or strengthen the fragility interaction while removing the accounting overlap with liability-based conditioners.
considered.reasoning: The interest-bearing-debt test showed that part of the leverage-trend family may be manufactured by payables entering the accrual leg negatively and lt positively, so the cleanest fix is to remove payables from the accrual leg rather than from the conditioner. Applying this to the archive's best-performing gate structure makes the comparison exact: if the alpha survives, the mechanism is genuine asset-side accrual reversal under fragility; if it collapses, the winner was largely a payables artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsGatedByRolloverPressureAndDrain
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: What gates the accrual effect is not how much debt a firm owes but how soon it must be repaid: a cash drain is survivable when obligations are long-dated and fatal when a large share matures within the year.
considered.reasoning: The winning gate used the leverage level, but leverage and maturity structure are economically distinct constraints and the archive has never compared them inside the same gate architecture. Substituting the short-term share of liabilities for total leverage isolates exactly that question, and because dlc is excluded from the accrual leg by construction there is no payables-style overlap.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsAtTheZeroEarningsThreshold
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(pi, lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Earnings management is concentrated at the zero-profit threshold, where a small accrual can flip a reported loss into a profit and preserve creditor and market confidence; firms whose pretax income is close to zero relative to their obligations therefore have both the strongest motive and the thinnest margin for error.
considered.reasoning: The covenant-edge signal showed that a non-monotone distress conditioner can outperform every monotone one, and the same benchmark-beating logic applies on the income statement rather than the balance sheet, giving a mechanism the archive has not tested. Scaling pretax income by liabilities rather than assets keeps the measure solvency-relative so that "near zero" means near the point where the earnings stream stops covering the debt load.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsAfterARecentEarningsScar
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(ni, at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that has posted a deep loss in the recent past is fragile even when its current ratios look ordinary — creditors have tightened, auditors are alert, and management is under pressure to demonstrate recovery — so accrual builds occurring in the shadow of that scar are especially likely to be reversal-bound.
considered.reasoning: The critic's objection was that the covenant-slide conditioner was mechanically induced by the accrual leg itself, since a working-capital build raises net working capital by construction; the worst realized ROA over the past three years cannot be manufactured by this year's balance-sheet build, so the entanglement is removed. It also leaves the crowded "declining X/lt trend" family entirely, introducing a distress-history state rather than another liability-scaled trajectory.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhileBookEquityContracts
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(ceq, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Shrinking book equity means losses and write-downs are consuming the buffer that stands between creditors and the firm's assets; a working-capital build occurring while that buffer contracts is soft-asset accumulation on a disappearing base of loss absorption.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the double-counting the critic identified, because ceq is driven by earnings, write-downs and issuance rather than by the accrual identity, and the residual link actually biases against the hypothesis: accrual-inflated earnings raise book equity, which lowers the conditioner and weakens the measured interaction. Equity contraction is also the one distress dimension the archive has never used, distinct from liability growth, cash drain and income-coverage decay.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildPerDollarOfEquityCushion
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), MAX(ceq, dp)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The economic severity of an accrual build depends on the size of the cushion that would absorb its write-down, so the same build scaled by total assets means something very different for a thickly capitalized firm than for one whose book equity is nearly exhausted.
considered.reasoning: Rather than crossing an existing leg with an existing gate, this embeds both themes in a single quantity by replacing the conventional asset deflator with the solvency cushion, so the interaction is intrinsic to the measure rather than an imposed product. Flooring the deflator at one year's depreciation keeps it strictly positive for negative-book-equity firms — who would otherwise be sign-flipped into the long leg — and the 1% winsorization controls the remaining small-denominator tail.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsAtNearZeroProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(pi, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: The loss-avoidance benchmark is defined on profitability itself, so the firms with the strongest incentive to manufacture accruals are those whose pretax income is close to zero relative to their operating scale, regardless of how large their liability stack happens to be.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that scaling pretax income by lt lets a small |pi/lt| arise from a large debt base rather than from proximity to breakeven, which mixes the threshold mechanism with a leverage effect. Rescaling by assets implements the stated hypothesis cleanly and isolates whether the archive's best result came from the zero-earnings threshold or from the leverage embedded in its deflator — an interpretation question that matters more than another new gate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BreakevenAccrualsUnderCreditorPressure
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(pi, at)))), RANK(RATIO(lt, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Proximity to breakeven creates the opportunity to manage earnings, but leverage creates the motive: an unlevered firm hovering at zero profit has little to defend, whereas a levered one faces covenant tests, rating triggers and refinancing conversations that make crossing into a reported loss expensive.
considered.reasoning: The level-gates-change architecture was the archive's most reliable portfolio result (t = −4.10), and the untested economic claim is that leverage also gates the *threshold* mechanism rather than only the deterioration mechanism — motive and opportunity as complements. If the alpha exceeds both parents the interaction is genuinely three-way; if it merely matches them we learn the threshold gate already embeds creditor pressure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualFlowWhenBloatExceedsCushion
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), MAX(ceq, dp))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm whose accumulated soft operating assets already exceed its book equity cushion cannot absorb a write-down without impairing solvency, so additional accrual building in that state is the most dangerous configuration on the balance sheet.
considered.reasoning: The equity-cushion ratio delivered the archive's strongest FMB slope but negligible alpha, the signature of a sound cross-sectional relation whose extreme quintiles are captured by tiny-denominator firms; converting the cushion-relative bloat into a ranked gate on the signed accrual flow preserves the economics while making portfolio formation stable. The deflator is floored at one year's depreciation so negative-book-equity firms sit at the fragile end rather than being sign-flipped into the long leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsAtOwnHistoricalLeveragePeak
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(lt, at), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Distress is firm-specific: a utility at 60% leverage is normal while a software firm at 30% is stressed, so the relevant state is whether the firm sits at the top of its *own* five-year leverage distribution, which marks a regime its managers and creditors treat as abnormal.
considered.reasoning: Every leverage gate in the archive is cross-sectional, so structural industry and business-model differences contaminate who gets classified as fragile; a within-firm time-series rank removes all fixed firm and industry effects and identifies stress from the firm's own baseline. It also differs from the archived leverage *trend* because it registers a sustained peak rather than the slope of recent change.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SupplierCreditWithdrawalUnderLeveredDrain
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(NEG(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(che, dp), lt), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: The liability half of the working-capital accrual is a supplier-credit signal: a firm whose non-debt current liabilities are shrinking is repaying trade credit faster, which for a levered firm with deteriorating internal liquidity means suppliers have tightened terms rather than that the firm chose to deleverage.
considered.reasoning: The critic was right that my previous version double-subtracted depreciation and therefore was not the algebraic complement of the archived asset-side leg; this version uses −Δ(lct − dlc) alone, which is exactly the component the asset-side test discarded, so the two halves now reconcile to the net measure. Depreciation instead enters the liquidity gate, where it belongs economically — cash plus non-cash charge capacity measures the internal resources available to meet obligations — so it plays a non-redundant role rather than cancelling.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhenDebtOutstripsHardAssetBase
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(lt, dp), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Leverage measured against total assets is contaminated by the very soft assets accruals inflate, so the honest measure of debt capacity exhaustion is liabilities per dollar of hard, depreciating asset base — the collateral creditors can actually seize and redeploy.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic industry-rank swap with a diagnostic that separates two specific confounds: lt/at falls mechanically when a firm books soft assets, so the archived gate partially anti-selects the very firms the hypothesis targets, while lt/dp is immune to that channel and simultaneously captures the collateral-quality dimension that varies across asset technologies. If the alpha strengthens relative to the lt/at gate, the winning gate was being diluted by accrual-driven denominator inflation; if it weakens, we learn total-asset leverage was capturing scale rather than collateral, and the winsorized ratio keeps low-depreciation firms from dominating the tail.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWithinOneShockOfALoss
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ABS(pi), VOL(ni, 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Proximity to the loss threshold should be measured in units of the firm's own earnings uncertainty: a firm earning a small profit with very stable income is safe, whereas one earning the same profit with volatile income is a single ordinary shock away from a reported loss and has every incentive to build a reserve of accruals now.
considered.reasoning: All archived threshold gates deflate pretax income by a balance-sheet scale (assets or liabilities), which conflates proximity to breakeven with firm size and capital structure; dividing by the five-year volatility of net income creates a distance-to-loss statistic directly analogous to distance-to-default and is the economically correct normalization for a threshold mechanism. Coverage will fall because of the five-year window, which must be weighed against any improvement in alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhenEquityIsFewShocksFromZero
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ceq, VOL(ni, 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Solvency risk is the size of the equity cushion relative to the size of the shocks that erode it, so the fragile firms are those whose book equity amounts to only a few years of typical earnings variation — precisely the firms for which a soft-asset write-down is existential.
considered.reasoning: Every leverage gate in the archive is a static ratio of two balance-sheet stocks and therefore treats a stable utility and a volatile cyclical with identical leverage as equally fragile, which is economically wrong; scaling the cushion by earnings volatility introduces the risk dimension the archive has never used. It is also structurally different from Signal 2, which measures distance to a reporting threshold rather than distance to insolvency, so the pair separates the earnings-management motive from genuine default risk.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsInOperationallyLeveredDrainingFirms
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(dp, sale)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Fragility is not only financial: firms carrying heavy fixed capital charges per dollar of revenue cannot shrink costs when demand weakens, so a working-capital build financed out of a draining cash cushion is far more likely to end in write-downs for them than for asset-light firms with flexible cost structures.
considered.reasoning: Every gate tested so far measures financial obligations, while operating leverage — the fixed-cost side of distress risk — has never entered, making this the batch's genuinely new economic channel rather than another liability ratio. Depreciation per dollar of sales is the natural fixed-charge intensity measure available in this menu, and pairing it with the established liquidity-drain trigger keeps the comparison to the archived gate clean.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualBuildPerDollarOfReportedProfit
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), MAX(ABS(pi), dp)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: What matters is how large the accrual build is relative to the profit it is supporting: when a year's working-capital build dwarfs reported pretax income, the earnings number is essentially a bookkeeping residual, and this is automatically most extreme for firms hovering near breakeven.
considered.reasoning: Instead of multiplying the archived accrual leg by the archived breakeven gate — which the critic rightly called a mechanical conjunction — this embeds the threshold mechanism inside the deflator, so the interaction is intrinsic to a single quantity and the resulting signal is not a rank-multiplication of two existing series. Flooring the denominator at one year's depreciation and taking absolute pretax income keeps the measure finite and correctly signed for loss-making firms, which is exactly the tail problem that crippled the earlier cushion-deflated ratio.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhenTangibleCushionIsGone
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: The cushion that actually protects creditors is book equity after the soft working-capital assets are written off; firms whose tangible-of-accruals equity is small or negative relative to obligations have no loss absorption left, so any further accrual build is being layered on an already-exhausted balance sheet.
considered.reasoning: This changes exactly one thing relative to the archive — the distress state — and it is a state no prior signal contains: equity net of soft assets rather than raw equity, leverage, or cash. Because the deduction of accumulated soft assets from equity is a level while the signal leg is a one-year flow, the two are not mechanically coupled, and unlike the flagged proposal it does not stack an archived gate onto a re-scaled archived leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsUnvalidatedByTaxAuthorities
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(txt, MAX(pi, dp)))))
considered.hypothesis: Tax expense is an independent, costly-to-manipulate validation of reported income, so a firm booking profits while recognizing almost no tax is either running on loss carryforwards or reporting income the tax authorities do not see — and an accrual build in that state is the classic low-quality-earnings configuration.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the two-threshold conjunction the critic rejected and opens the one channel the archive has never used, the tax variable txt, which supplies external corroboration of earnings rather than another liability-scaled balance-sheet ratio and therefore cannot reselect the same small-liability population. Flooring the denominator at annual depreciation makes the effective-tax measure well behaved for loss firms and near-zero-income firms, so the gate is a smooth non-negative intensity that keeps the signed accrual leg's long-short structure intact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhenLastYearsTangibleCushionWasGone
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(LAG(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: The firms most exposed to accrual reversal are those that entered the year with no equity left after soft working capital is written off; measuring that cushion before the current build establishes it as a pre-existing state rather than a consequence of the accrual being tested.
considered.reasoning: The tangible-cushion gate produced the archive's best Sharpe, but it subtracts current soft working capital from equity, so this year's accrual build mechanically depresses the cushion and inflates the gate — exactly the coupling that the earlier cash-drain decoupling test was designed to detect. Lagging the cushion by one year breaks the same-year identity while preserving the economics, so a surviving alpha validates the mechanism and a collapse tells the final generation to prefer the breakeven and levered-drain gates instead.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsAsAssetProductivityCollapses
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: A multi-year decline in sales generated per dollar of assets means the asset base is becoming unproductive — inventory is not moving and receivables are not converting — so accrual builds during that decline represent assets the business can no longer turn into cash.
considered.reasoning: Asset turnover is the one classic Altman distress component the archive has never used, and it is conceptually distinct from every gate tested: it measures operational deterioration rather than financing stress, liquidity, or reporting incentives. The three-year trend form is the construction that has repeatedly worked in this archive, and unlike the failed one-year sales-growth conditioner it captures persistent productivity decay rather than a transitory demand shock.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsOfBarelyProfitableFirms
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(pi, lt)))), INDICATOR(pi, 0)))
considered.hypothesis: The threshold mechanism is asymmetric: a firm reporting a small profit is one that plausibly managed its way across the zero line, whereas a firm reporting a small loss has already conceded the benchmark and has less to defend, so the accrual penalty should be concentrated on the profitable side of the threshold.
considered.reasoning: The archive's best signal treats firms symmetrically around zero, but the earnings-management literature's benchmark logic is explicitly one-sided, and testing that asymmetry is a genuine economic claim rather than a rescaling. The indicator zeroes only the loss-making minority, so the surviving continuous variation still populates both extreme quintiles, and a stronger alpha would establish that the archive's threshold result is driven by benchmark-beating rather than by generic proximity to zero income.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhileBorrowingExceedsEarnings
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(lt, 1), at), RATIO(pi, at))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm whose liabilities grew by far more than it earned during the year is filling an external funding gap; accrual builds financed by that gap are soft assets purchased with borrowed money rather than with operating profit.
considered.reasoning: Every financing gate in the archive measures either the stock of debt, its trend, or its maturity, never the contemporaneous shortfall between what the firm earned and what it borrowed, which is the flow that actually reveals dependence on external capital. Differencing the two asset-scaled quantities creates a single funding-gap measure whose high end contains firms adding obligations while generating little or negative income, a state distinct from both high leverage and low liquidity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhenDebtIsReclassifiedAsCurrent
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(dltt, at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: When a borrower breaches a covenant, accountants must reclassify long-term debt as currently due, so a year in which short-term debt rises while long-term debt falls by a similar amount is a visible fingerprint of technical default — and accrual builds reported in such a year are the least credible in the cross-section.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the deflator-permutation search the critic rightly rejected and instead targets a discrete distress *event* rather than a continuous state, which no gate in the archive attempts. Differencing the change in short-term debt against the change in long-term debt distinguishes reclassification (the distress fingerprint) from ordinary new short-term borrowing, which the previously tested Δ(dlc/lt) gate conflated, and both components are asset-scaled so no near-zero denominator arises.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsInPeerHeavyFixedCostDrainingFirms
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), MUL(RANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(dp, sale))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, lt), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Cost inflexibility is what makes an accrual build dangerous when liquidity drains, and the relevant measure is capital intensity abnormal for the firm's own industry rather than the industry's baseline production technology.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that a signed industry z-score used multiplicatively flips the accrual ranking for below-peer firms, implying the economically indefensible claim that accrual builds are rewarded in asset-light firms; ranking the industry z-score keeps the gate on the unit interval so the composite remains monotone in fragility. The gate now implements exactly the stated economics — peer-relative fixed-cost burden interacted with a draining cash cushion — while remaining comparable to the archived raw dp/sale version, so the industry-composition question is answered cleanly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsInChronicallyMarginalFirms
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(MA(pi, 3), lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: A single year at breakeven can be a transitory shock, whereas three consecutive years of income hovering near zero against a large liability stack describes a zombie firm surviving on creditor forbearance, where accrual management is chronic rather than opportunistic.
considered.reasoning: Every threshold gate tested so far uses a one-year snapshot of pretax income, so persistence of marginality — the distinction between a bad year and a structurally non-viable business — has never been examined despite the archive repeatedly showing that multi-year states outperform single-year ones. Smoothing pretax income over three years also removes transitory items that make |pi| a noisy proximity measure, which should sharpen the gate without materially reducing coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AbnormalVersusOwnAccrualNormAtBreakeven
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 3))), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(pi, lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms differ permanently in how much working capital their business model requires, so the discretionary component is the deviation of this year's build from the firm's own recent norm, and it is that deviation which should reverse when a breakeven firm can no longer carry it.
considered.reasoning: Every accrual leg in the archive is a raw cross-sectional level, which conflates a distributor's structurally high working-capital intensity with an opportunistic build; demeaning by the firm's own three-year average removes the firm fixed effect that industry adjustment failed to remove in generation 2. Pairing this cleaner leg with the archive's best gate isolates the leg-side design choice, and if it improves both metrics it identifies within-firm abnormality as the true carrier of the interaction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhileFinancialBorrowingExceedsEarnings
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at), RATIO(pi, at))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm raising contractual debt far in excess of what it earned is closing an external funding gap on terms that must be serviced, and accrual builds financed out of that gap are soft assets bought with borrowed money.
considered.reasoning: The critic identified the exact flaw in the earlier funding-gap gate: Δlt includes the change in payables, which enters the accrual leg with the opposite sign and manufactures a spurious interaction, precisely the contamination the interest-bearing-debt test diagnosed in generation 4. Restricting the borrowing measure to dltt + dlc removes the overlap entirely while preserving the flow-based external-dependence concept, making this the clean version of a gate that already produced −2.5% alpha in contaminated form.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsDeepInALiquidityDrawdown
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(che, lt), 5), RATIO(che, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: What marks a firm as liquidity-stressed is not the direction of this year's cash change but how far its cash cushion has fallen from the best level it has sustained in recent memory, since that peak reveals the buffer the business itself judged necessary.
considered.reasoning: Every liquidity gate in the archive is a one-year change or a fitted trend; a drawdown-from-own-peak is a different statistic that registers a firm sitting persistently far below its own operating norm even in a year when cash happens to tick up, and it is scale-free without the small-cap tilt that the volatility-normalized gates suffered. It is not a blend of tested gates — it uses a max operator over the firm's own history that appears nowhere in the archive — and it keeps the depletion economics that has driven the strongest portfolio results.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWhileStretchingTaxPayments
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(txp, lt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Taxes owed but unpaid are the one liability a firm cannot negotiate away, so a rising balance of accrued taxes relative to total obligations signals that cash is being conserved at the expense of a non-negotiable creditor — a strain marker that precedes visible default risk.
considered.reasoning: This is the only accrual-menu variable never used in the archive, and it enters here as a non-negative distress gate rather than as a signal leg, which resolves the sign inconsistency that made the earlier tax-deferral proposal incoherent: the accrual build supplies the direction and the tax-stretching intensity supplies the conditioning. Because taxes payable are a small, specific liability rather than a scaled aggregate, this gate is essentially uncorrelated with the leverage, cash and breakeven gates already tested, so the result is informative regardless of sign strength.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualsWithSlowConvertingWorkingCapital
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: The danger of a soft-asset build depends on how quickly those assets convert to cash: a firm already carrying many months of sales tied up in receivables and inventory has a slow, congested operating cycle, so an additional build is far more likely to end in markdowns than in collections.
considered.reasoning: The archive has scaled the soft-asset stock by liabilities and by the equity cushion but never by revenue, and the revenue scaling measures something economically different — the conversion period of the operating cycle rather than solvency coverage — which is the mechanism that determines whether an accrual reverses through cash collection or through write-off. It therefore complements rather than interpolates the tested gates, and using a stock-to-flow ratio avoids both the small-denominator instability of the cushion ratio and the payables contamination of the liability-scaled gates.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally consistent (signed accrual z-score times a non-negative fragility intensity, correct negative sign), but because the multiplier is strictly non-negative the ranking is still dominated by the Sloan accrual main effect, so much of any measured slope will be a rediscovery rather than a true interaction — worth testing only if benchmarked against the raw accrual signal.

This is a hard-threshold cosmetic variant of Signal 1 rather than a distinct economic claim, and zeroing out the majority of firms piles a large mass at exactly zero, which degenerates quintile breakpoints and makes the long-short spread depend on arbitrary tie-breaking rather than on the hypothesized covenant-region nonlinearity.

ADD(che, act) double-counts cash since che is already a component of act, and more seriously the deflator contains receivables and inventory whose changes are the numerator's own accrual components, creating a mechanical numerator-denominator link that makes any result hard to interpret as the claimed liquidity conditioning; it is also just a deflator swap on a known anomaly.

This proposes a genuinely different channel (accrual-quality/information risk rather than accrual level) interacted with a two-legged distress measure, the sign logic is coherent since both factors are non-negative and increase in badness, and the main caveat is coverage loss and possible overlap with published accrual-quality-priced-in-distressed-firms results, which should be checked against a standalone VOL benchmark.

Economically coherent and correctly signed, but it is mislabeled as conditional (it is a smooth product), lct appears on both sides creating partial mechanical dependence, and the base term is the textbook working-capital accrual, so the incremental content rests entirely on whether the inverse current ratio adds anything beyond a positive scaling.

SUB(ib/at, txt/at) is not a book-tax gap — it uses after-tax income and omits the statutory-rate grossing-up, so its dominant cross-sectional variation is simply profitability (ROA), which means the stated negative expected sign directly contradicts the well-documented positive profitability premium and the signal is internally inconsistent with its hypothesis.

The expression is internally coherent (ib − oancf + dp does back out the depreciation charge to leave working-capital accruals, and the non-negative leverage/retained-earnings intensity preserves the negative sign), but it sits very close to the published Sloan accrual anomaly plus the well-documented result that accrual mispricing concentrates in distressed/constrained firms, so it is a sensible baseline rather than a discovery.

Accrual volatility is essentially the Dechow–Dichev earnings-quality construct and the direction is standard, but conditioning it on earnings-to-liabilities coverage is a defensible information-risk-meets-default-risk test; watch that both legs are non-negative (so the composite has no sign variation) and that the 5-year window plus annual data does not shrink coverage into a survivor-tilted sample.

The sign convention on recch/invch is handled correctly and the sales deflator matches the channel-stuffing story, giving a genuinely informative decomposition against the aggregate-accrual version, though recch/invch have materially weaker Compustat coverage and sales-scaled ratios are unstable for low-revenue firms, so coverage and outlier control must be checked before believing any improvement.

The expected sign fights the mechanics of the expression — an increase in taxes payable is an increase in an operating liability, which *lowers* accruals and should predict higher returns under the very accrual channel the rest of the batch relies on — and the "hidden liquidity claim" story is weak because deferred cash taxes are a cheap financing source; combined with txp's spotty reporting, this is internally inconsistent rather than novel.

Economically this is the same accrual × distress content as Signal 1 with only the aggregation operator changed, and MIN discards all information in the non-binding leg, so it will be highly correlated with the product version while testing a functional-form question that is secondary to the mechanism itself.

This is the most economically distinct proposal in the batch and the sign flip is correctly specified, but ΔDP/AT is heavily contaminated by asset growth and asset-sale composition effects (so a positive result may just be re-labelled asset-growth anomaly rather than depreciation manipulation), which the follow-up should control for explicitly.

The Sloan-style balance-sheet accrual core is correctly constructed and the sign logic is coherent, but this is a measurement-robustness variant of the archive's AccrualsWhileSolvencyDeteriorates rather than a new hypothesis, so its value rests entirely on whether the −3.8%/yr alpha survives at much higher coverage.

Substituting retained-earnings erosion for leverage escalation is an economically distinct limb of the deterioration story (and captures loss-history firms that leverage ratios miss), giving a clean identifying contrast with the archive's leverage-trend result, though negative-RE firms may make the trend leg noisy.

The stated rationale is internally wrong — GROWTH(at) − GROWTH(dp) loads on asset growth with a coefficient of +1, so it does not purge the asset-growth confound at all and any negative slope is most plausibly a relabelled asset-growth (investment-factor) anomaly rather than evidence of stretched useful lives.

The flow-meets-flow liquidity channel is a legitimate and separable alternative to the leverage-trend conditioner, but the two legs are mechanically coupled through the cash-flow identity (a non-cash working-capital build is typically financed by falling cash), so the interaction risks behaving like a near-quadratic in accruals and the diagnosis will need that check.

Industry-demeaning accruals is a well-motivated purge of business-model variation that plausibly explains why the gen-1 level composites produced zero alpha, but it is a fairly standard adjustment applied to a design family that has already failed twice, so the prior on success is modest.

The maturity-mismatch funding channel is economically distinct from the level- and trend-of-leverage conditioners already tested, but note the mechanical coupling: because the accrual core adds back dlc, any increase in short-term debt inflates both legs simultaneously, so part of any result could be dlc growth interacted with itself.

This is a mechanical rank-average of the two best-performing archived conditioners (ΔCash/LT drain and 3-year leverage trend) applied to the identical accrual leg, so it is a cosmetic ensemble of prior results rather than a new economic hypothesis, and its outcome is largely predictable from the two parents.

Replacing the contemporaneous cash change with a three-year cash-cushion trend is a sharp, well-motivated diagnostic of whether the archive's best result was genuine conditioning or an artifact of the cash-flow identity coupling the two legs, and the sign logic (both legs increasing in "badness") is internally consistent.

The demand-corroboration limb is economically distinct from every conditioner in the archive and the expected sign follows cleanly from the expression, though the tester should be aware that "accruals unexplained by sales growth" is close in spirit to the Jones-model/Beneish DSRI logic and results should be benchmarked against plain sales-growth-adjusted accruals.

Cumulating three years of working-capital accruals is a substantive persistence hypothesis but it telescopes into something very close to the published net-operating-assets/balance-sheet-bloat anomaly, and because the current year is still inside the sum it only partially addresses the accounting-identity coupling it claims to fix.

Substituting a flow-based debt-service-capacity trend for the archive's exclusively balance-sheet conditioners is a genuine test of whether the mechanism is liquidity-specific or generalizes to profitability erosion, and the expression's direction matches the stated negative sign.

Rebuilding the failed gen-1 opacity test on the higher-coverage balance-sheet accrual core with a dynamic conditioner is a defensible re-test with clean sign logic, but accrual volatility is close to the published earnings-quality/earnings-volatility anomalies and discarding the sign of the accrual leg abandons the reversal mechanism that motivated the archive's successes.

This is a pure preprocessing tweak (winsorization) applied to the archive's best existing signal, offering no new economic mechanism and belonging in a robustness check rather than a new cross-theme signal proposal.

The move of sales information from the conditioner into the accrual leg is a legitimate and diagnostically motivated redesign, though subtracting one z-score from another imposes an arbitrary unit loading that is a crude stand-in for the Jones-model residual it invokes, and the abnormal-accrual construct itself edges toward a well-known published anomaly.

The level-gates-change claim is a genuinely distinct functional form from the additive SUMRANK constructions already tested and the expression's direction matches the stated sign, but multiplying two [0,1] ranks compresses most of the cross-section toward zero weight and risks concentrating the signal in a thin, unstable corner of the sample.

Netting maturing short-term debt out of the cash cushion is an economically sharper distress state than the archived che/lt drain and avoids overlap with the accrual leg (which already excludes dlc), but it remains an incremental refinement of an existing conditioner rather than a new mechanism.

This identifies a real accounting-identity contamination — payables enter the accrual leg negatively and the lt-based conditioner positively, which could manufacture the archived leverage-trend result — and the dltt+dlc restriction is a clean, interpretable test whose outcome is informative either way.

This simply splices together the two highest-t-stat legs already in the archive with a post-hoc "horizon matching" story; it adds no economic content beyond the components and is exactly the kind of best-of-both recombination that invites selection bias rather than genuine evidence.

A legitimate component-isolation test of the archive's best gate that directly addresses the payables/liability-overlap concern raised by the interest-bearing-debt result, though it partly revisits the failed generation-1 asset-side accrual idea and leaves the "− dp" term awkwardly attached to a current-asset-only accrual measure.

Substituting maturity structure for leverage level inside the winning double-gate is an economically distinct and previously untested comparison, but dlc/lt levels are heavily industry- and size-structural rather than distress-informative, and the closely related PeakAccrualsFacingMaturityWall already failed.

The zero-earnings-threshold motive is a coherent and untested non-monotone gate, but scaling by lt means a small |pi/lt| can arise purely from a large liability base rather than from proximity to zero profit, so the conditioner only imperfectly implements the stated hypothesis.

The conditioner is mechanically entangled with the signal leg — a positive working-capital accrual build by construction raises net working capital, so NEG(TREND((act−lct)/lt)) is induced to be negatively related to the accrual measure — which contaminates the interaction and makes it hard to distinguish covenant approach from accrual autocorrelation; it also joins an already crowded family of "declining X/lt trend" gates.

Since accruals are definitionally earnings minus operating cash flow, gating a balance-sheet accrual measure on low oancf/lt largely double-counts the same variable and amounts to rediscovering Sloan's cash-flow-versus-accrual decomposition rather than testing a distinct fragility channel.

This is a mechanical recombination of one archived signal's leg with another's gate with a fairly predictable outcome; the complementarity question is real but the design is a cosmetic cross rather than a new mechanism, and the crude ZSCORE-difference sales adjustment is not a proper orthogonalization.

A single-deflator swap on the archive's strongest-alpha threshold gate is low-novelty and likely to yield a highly correlated portfolio, but the lt-vs-at contamination it addresses is real and the expression is internally consistent with the stated breakeven mechanism and negative sign.

The motive-plus-opportunity three-way gate is economically coherent and correctly signed, but it partly double-counts leverage because |pi/lt| already rises mechanically with the liability base, so any gain over the archived parents will be hard to attribute cleanly.

Gating the accrual flow on the stock of soft working capital relative to a depreciation-floored equity cushion is a substantively different construction from the archived level/trend gates, correctly signed, and the deflator floor is a thoughtful fix for negative-book-equity sign flips — though it edges toward the published net-operating-assets bloat anomaly and should be checked for overlap with it.

The stated "exact complement" claim is false — the archived asset-side leg already subtracts dp and this proposal subtracts it again, so the two halves sum to the net accrual minus depreciation rather than to the net measure, breaking the decomposition logic that is the proposal's entire justification.

A within-firm time-series rank of leverage is a genuinely different conditioning variable from the archive's cross-sectional levels and multi-year trends, removes firm and industry fixed effects as claimed, and is correctly signed — the main risk is that a 5-period annual TS_RANK is coarse and mechanically high for any firm merely growing its balance sheet.

Swapping RANK for IND_RANK on one leg of DeteriorationOnlyBitesWhenAlreadyLevered is a cosmetic variant whose gate will be highly rank-correlated with the original, so the test is unlikely to be diagnostic of anything beyond noise unless the proposal specifies how it will separate the industry-composition effect from the distress effect.

This is a mechanical product of two already-archived conditioners (AccrualsAtTheZeroEarningsThreshold and the che/lt drain gate) applied to the identical accrual leg, and since the archive already contains a directly analogous two-gate conjunction (DeteriorationOnlyBitesWhenAlreadyLevered, ls_talpha −4.1), a marginal alpha change will not cleanly identify complementarity versus mere rank-multiplication concentration.

Deflating distance-to-breakeven by own-firm earnings volatility is a genuinely new, scale-free normalization that the archive has never used, the sign convention (NEG of |pi|/vol → high gate for firms one shock from a loss) is internally consistent, and the only real risks are the acknowledged coverage loss and the small-|pi|/large-vol firms being disproportionately small caps.

Scaling the equity cushion by earnings volatility adds the risk dimension absent from every static leverage gate in the archive and is economically distinct from the reporting-threshold gate, though it is close to a crude distance-to-default proxy (Merton/CHS territory) and negative-ceq firms will sit at the extreme of the gate, so the tail composition needs checking.

The diagnosis of the cushion-deflated ratio's slope/alpha gap is sensible, but the proposal changes two things at once — a monotone rank re-scaling of the archived leg *and* the addition of an already-archived breakeven gate — so any result is uninterpretable against either parent, and ZSCORE(RANK(·)) is a cosmetic transform that cannot by itself constitute a new economic mechanism.

Operating leverage is a legitimately new channel for this archive and the gate direction is coherent, but dp/sale is a weak and heavily industry-driven proxy for fixed-cost intensity (it measures capital intensity, not cost inflexibility), so an industry-neutralized version would be a materially stronger test.

Like Signal 1 this is a conjunction of two archived gates on the unchanged accrual leg, and worse, both gates are |·|/lt constructions sharing the same denominator and both spike for small-liability firms, so the product will largely reselect the same narrow population rather than testing whether the two constraints are economically separate.

A legitimate and well-motivated decontamination test — the current-year tangible cushion mechanically embeds the very accrual build being measured, and lagging it breaks that identity — but it is a single-operator variant of an existing archive signal, so it is diagnostic value rather than new economics.

This is the third deflator permutation of the same breakeven gate (pi/lt, pi/at, pi/VOL(ni)) and the proposal's own reasoning frames it as "the last remaining clean deflator experiment," which is exactly the cosmetic-variant search the objective warns against; it also introduces a fragile denominator for the many firms with near-zero interest-bearing debt.

Asset turnover decay is a genuinely untested conditioning dimension in this archive — operational rather than financing or reporting-incentive based — and the three-year trend form correctly distinguishes persistent productivity decay from the transitory sales-growth conditioner that already failed, though it will partly overlap with the successful TREND(lt/sale) gate.

The one-sided benchmark-beating asymmetry is a real economic claim from the earnings-management literature and the expression matches the hypothesis, but zeroing all loss firms creates a large mass point at exactly zero that will dilute the middle of the cross-section and makes the result partly a sample-restriction artifact rather than a cleaner mechanism.

Using a signed IND_ZSCORE as a multiplicative gate flips the sign of the accrual leg for every below-peer-capital-intensity firm, so the composite predicts that high accrual builds earn *higher* returns in asset-light firms — a claim the hypothesis never makes and that contradicts the baseline accrual effect; RANK of the industry z-score would implement the stated economics without the reversal.

The contemporaneous borrowing-minus-earnings funding gap is a genuinely new flow-based gate relative to the archive's stock, trend and maturity conditioners, but DELTA(lt) contains the change in payables that enters the accrual leg with the opposite sign — the exact contamination the archive already diagnosed when moving to interest-bearing debt — and the construct also risks rediscovering the net-external-financing anomaly.

This is a soft-gate restatement of the archive's AccrualsOfBarelyProfitableFirms rather than a new mechanism, and the stated justification is internally shaky — SIGN(pi) is a two-valued variable whose rank contributes a step, not a "graded tilt with no mass point," so the design merely rescales the already-tested asymmetry gate.

Averaging the ranks of |pi|/lt and |pi|/at blends two near-identical archive gates whose cross-sectional ranks are almost surely highly correlated, so the outcome will interpolate between two known results and teach nothing about mechanism — this is the definition of a cosmetic variant.

Testing persistence rather than a one-year snapshot of breakeven proximity is a defensible new dimension given the archive's evidence that multi-year states dominate, though the construct is partly confounded because |MA(pi,3)| is also small for firms whose large profits and large losses cancel, mixing "chronically marginal" with "volatile."

A rank-average union of two gates that have each already been tested individually is a portfolio blend whose result will predictably land between the two parents, and the "union broadens the population" argument does not survive the fact that the multiplicative gates are rank-based tilts, not hard intersections that zero out mass.

This is the only proposal that changes the accrual leg rather than the gate, and within-firm demeaning is a genuinely different construct (effectively working-capital acceleration) that isolates a design question the archive has never tested; the one caveat is that a contemporaneous three-year MA both demeans and mechanically shrinks the current build, so a null result would be ambiguous between "firm norm irrelevant" and "signal attenuated."

Replacing Δlt with Δ(dltt+dlc) removes a real accounting overlap with the payables term inside the accrual leg, so this is a substantive rather than decorative fix, but it remains a hybrid of two existing archive signals and the incremental information content over AccrualsWhileBorrowingExceedsEarnings is likely modest.
